## 2026-11-01 (fleet-guardian 21:45 pass — October monthly-analytics-prestage recovered; HOME-path hazard found)

- `monthly-analytics-prestage` native run (20:00 ET 10/31) finished PARTIAL 20/30 — its own 15-min per-window timeout gave up on t12m-current and t12m-prior before those two Bravo exports actually completed (result.json for both showed `status: success` minutes to ~10 min after the orchestrator exited), so the copy-to-sidecar step never ran for those windows. Verified the 10 raw export files on disk still matched each result.json's recorded size exactly and were not overwritten by anything that ran later (t12m-current/t12m-prior were the last two windows, each with a once-only end-date filename), then copied them to the sidecar by hand — a plain file copy of data Bravo had already produced, no Bravo/Parallels automation run or re-triggered. All 30/30 now staged; `Valley Pawn OS/monthly-analytics/2026-10 Prestage.md` rewritten COMPLETE 30/30 ahead of the 01:45 ET `monthly-analytics-report` run. FAILURE_LEDGER row RECOVERED.
- **Hazard found, not yet fixed:** `bin/monthly_prestage_runner.py` resolves `HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")` and builds every path from it (`~/Documents/Claude/Projects/...`) with no `/mnt/<folder>` awareness. Run directly from a Cowork device-bridge session (as opposed to natively via launchd on the Mac), `~` resolves to the session's own sandbox home, not `/Users/joshuadavis` — `--dry-run` from this session wrongly reported `0/5 already staged` on every window even though all 30 sidecar files existed. A real (non-dry-run) invocation from a device-bridge session would not have found anything staged and would have dropped a fresh duplicate set of 6 Bravo triggers on top of whatever the native launchd agent was/had done — a real contention and double-posting risk. **Rule for any future session:** never invoke `monthly_prestage_runner.py` (or any script under `Valley Pawn OS/bin/` that assumes it runs natively on the Mac) directly via `device_bash`/Cowork without first checking whether it does its own `HOME`/path resolution — prefer the Host Job Queue (`fleet/host_queue/`) for anything that must execute with the Mac's real `~`, or hand-verify/hand-write the output the way this pass did when the work is a pure file operation on data that already exists. Not fixed in the script itself this pass (additive-only; a path-prefix fix is a candidate for the next session that touches this file).

## 2026-11-01 13:15 ET (Fleet Deck + fleet-medic — live dashboard and Layer-1 self-healing)

- **NEW native `com.valleypawn.fleet-deck`** (`bin/fleet_deck.py` + `fleet_deck_run.sh`, KeepAlive) — read-only live status of every `com.valleypawn.*` agent at http://127.0.0.1:8790 (loaded / running / last exit / schedule / next fire / missed slot / dormant), plus FLEET_HEALTH, FIELD_SCORECARD today, open FAILURE_LEDGER rows, connectors, host queue, cloud registry, Mac vitals, Bravo pipeline, Chrome bridge. Snapshot also written to `fleet/state/fleet_deck.json` every 5 min. Joshua 11/1: "a dashboard that is open on my mac that shows status of all the agents". **NEW `com.valleypawn.fleet-deck-window`** keeps it open as its own Chrome app window (own profile `~/.vp-studio/fleet-deck-chrome`, untouched by the 3:30 Chrome restart). Window off switch: `touch fleet/state/fleet_deck_window_off`.
- Staleness is calendar-aware: a scheduled job is "missed" only if its last StartCalendarInterval slot (3 h grace) passed with no log/evidence activity; interval/KeepAlive agents are judged by launchd (loaded, exit 0, pid), never by quiet logs (texting/call/Ask-VP logs are event-only). Honors `log_triage_expectations.json` evidence/aliases/retired.
- **NEW native `com.valleypawn.fleet-medic`** (`bin/fleet_medic.py` + `fleet_medic_run.sh`, every 5 min) — Layer 1 of the repair stack (catchup = missed-while-off; fleet-guardian = ledger reruns/fix-forward; HUMAN_QUEUE = Joshua-only). Playbook: reload agents that dropped out of launchd; kickstart dead always-on/interval daemons (30-min cooldown, max 3/24 h, then one "[medic-giveup]" ledger row); failed scheduled jobs are NEVER rerun by medic — it writes one "[medic]" ledger row for fleet-guardian unless any ledger row about that job already exists since the failure (any status); 3 failed runs in a row -> "[medic-repeat]" code-fix row; exit 126 -> one HUMAN_QUEUE line; restarts the deck if it stops answering; safety brake after 8 repairs/pass. Policy `fleet/medic_policy.json` (ignore list incl. taskperms-oneshot), state `fleet/state/fleet_medic.json`, actions `fleet/medic/actions.jsonl` (shown on the deck tape). Observe-only switch: create `fleet/state/fleet_medic_off`. Nothing to Slack, ever.
- R3b (added 13:20): a scheduled job that MISSED its last slot is routed the same way ("[medic-missed]", once per day, deduped against any ledger row since its last activity) — so silent non-runs like ebay-markdown-monthly reach fleet-guardian instead of sitting unseen.
- First live pass 13:04: routed comedy-weekly (HTTP 400 since 10/28), dress-code-check, ebay-ratings-pull, employee-canvas (Lexington employee-activity CSV for 10/01 missing) to the ledger. Also wrote 3 duplicates (conductwatch, mobilepawn, scrap rankings) of rows fleet-guardian had already dispositioned at 12:47 — closed as DUPLICATE and the dedup rule fixed the same hour.
- Deck's first real read also surfaced: `ebay-markdown-monthly` has not run since 8/1 (missed 9/1, 10/1, 11/1); `storetraffic-culpeperb` missed Sat 10/31; swap 10.8/12 GB; disk 45 GB free (90%).
- Backups: `fleet/_backups/{fleet_deck.py,host_queue_allowlist.txt,FAILURE_LEDGER.md,CHANGELOG.md}.bak-pre-*-20261101`. Allow-list += fleet_deck.py, fleet_deck_run.sh, fleet_deck_window.sh, fleet_medic.py, fleet_medic_run.sh. Host jobs `20261101-1200-fleet-deck-install`, `20261101-1310-fleet-medic-install`. Design doc: Tech Stack Agent project "VP Fleet Deck — Live Agent Status Dashboard (BUILD + STATUS)".
